title: Signal-fusion A/B framework & safety dashboard for batching/caching configs
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build an experimentation and A/B testing framework focused on batching + KV-cache configuration changes. This ticket creates a signal-fusion metric stack and a safety-first dashboard and automation that allow safe canary applies, continuous ramping, and automated rollback if composite health/cost signals deviate from acceptance criteria. Unlike previous pure-cost or pure-latency experiments, this effort fuses multiple signals (cost per token, p50/p95 latency, model-quality regressions on eval prompts, hallucination rate, error rate, and user-visible timeouts) into a single decision pipeline with explainable component contributions.
rationale: We frequently see oscillation between aggressive batching for cost and conservative configs for latency/quality. Current experimentation artifacts are scattered; we need a unified signal and playbook that allows safe automation, faster iteration, and clearer postmortems. Signal fusion helps detect brittle false-positives (e.g., transient latency spike unrelated to config change) and surfaces root causes earlier.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment platform can run randomized rollout for a config_id and tag requests consistently
Dashboard exposes composite safety score, component contributions, per-cohort uplift for cost/latency/quality
Automated canary automation will pause/reroll when any guardrail trips (configured thresholds and sequential-test p-value spending)
Post-run report generated automatically with statistical summary, uplift, CIs, and suggested rollback reason
Synthetic traffic harness can reproduce experiment workload and replay customer-like cohorts
tasks: Design composite signal: weighted vector of cost_per_1k_tokens, p95_latency, eval_accuracy_delta, hallucination_rate, error_rate
Implement request tagging: add config_id & cohort_id to tracing/span and metrics pipeline
Add sequential testing backend: support alpha-spending and Bayesian posterior checks for early stopping
Build dashboard panes: cohort list, composite score timeseries, component waterfall, rollback events log, and cohort heatmap
Hook up canary apply automation: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% ramp with automated gate checks
Create synthetic load generator and traffic-replay job for reproducible tests
Write playbook for on-call/operator escalation and manual rollback steps
metrics: model_hallucination_rate (% of hallucinations on eval set)
dashboard_panels: Composite safety score timeline with anomaly shading
Per-cohort uplift table (cost/latency/quality) with CI columns
Waterfall chart: contribution of each signal to safety score changes
Sequential-test visualization: cumulative alpha spent and stop/continue decision
Rollback event stream with links to triggered metrics and traces
Cohort drift heatmap (traffic feature distributions vs baseline)
Synthetic vs production overlay for key metrics (sanity check)
decisions: Use a hybrid testing strategy: primary sequential frequentist checks (alpha-spending) + Bayesian posterior for probability-of-harm estimates
Composite safety score will be linear combination with explainable weights defaulted to: latency 35%, cost 25%, quality 30%, errors 10% (configurable per-experiment)
Automated ramp stops if any single component crosses its hard threshold OR composite score drops >10% absolute
Feature-flag service (LaunchDarkly or internal FF) will drive config rollout; config_id must be immutable during an experiment
Sample 100% of canary cohort for traces but sample metrics at 10% to conserve ingestion costs; ensure trace-linked sampling to metrics by id
